claim: A nonsingular 2x2 cross block A[I,J] alone forces bounded density for the four-coordinate quadratic form, without a condition on the pivot-side principal block.
counterexample: For independent Uniform[-1/2,1/2] variables, Q=(X1+Y1)^2-(X2+Y2)^2 has cross block diag(1,-1) but an unbounded logarithmic density at zero; the full matrix has only two nonzero eigenvalues 2 and -2, so this does not refute the owner target.
safe_replacement: QFORM-MULTIPIVOT-BILINEAR-SMALLBALL-v1: if disjoint I,J have equal size m>=2, A[I,I]=0, and A[I,J] is invertible, then ||p_Q||_infinity <= m/(m-1) |det A[I,J]|^{-1/m}.
